item.title: Angie Nixon Notches Another Win for the Left Through Old-Fashioned Organizing
item.description: State Representative Angie Nixon scored a stunning upset on Tuesday in Florida’s Democratic Senate primary. Her victory will test the strength of a democratic socialist in a red state.
item.dc:creator: Patricia Mazzei
item.media:credit: Saul Martinez for The New York Times
item.media:description: State Representative Angie Nixon of Florida easily defeated her more moderate opponent in the Democratic primary for Senate.

item.title: A Stunning Win for the Left in Florida: 6 Takeaways From Tuesday’s Primaries
item.description: State Representative Angie Nixon, a progressive firebrand, defeated a moderate who dramatically out-raised her with grass-roots enthusiasm. Can it carry her to victory in November?
item.dc:creator: Patricia Mazzei
item.media:credit: Saul Martinez for The New York Times
item.media:description: State Representative Angie Nixon spent just $60,000 on television advertising, compared to opponent Alex Vindman’s $2.2 million.

item.title: Mary Peltola and Dan Sullivan Advance in Key Alaska Senate Contest
item.description: Both parties see Alaska as key to winning the Senate. The state’s nonpartisan primary put Mary Peltola, a Democratic former congresswoman, on the same ballot as Dan Sullivan, the incumbent Republican she hopes to unseat. Both advanced to the general election.
item.dc:creator: Kellen Browning and Bayliss Wagner
item.media:credit: Kerry Tasker/Reuters; Eric Lee for The New York Times
item.media:description: Former Representative Mary Peltola, a Democrat, and Senator Dan Sullivan, a Republican, will advance to the general election for an Alaska Senate seat.
